newsitem.title: FRANCE: French grain sales to EU hit record in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: French grain sales to EU hit record in 1996/97.

text.p: France broke its record for grain exports to the rest of the European Union in the past year, selling a projected 19.2 million tonnes in the 12-month campaign to end on June 30, French cereals office ONIC said on Wednesday.
The volume exceeds last year's performance by 9.7 percent and beats a previous 1992 record of 15.9 million tonnes.

ONIC officials presenting a monthly supply/demand report said strong consumption across the 15-nation EU mainly accounted for the increase, with 61 percent of the EU's domestic demand destined for animal consumption.
However, an unknown quantity of grain leaving France may be earmarked for eventual export the world market through the Benelux countries.
In its report, ONIC revised up its projection for barley exports to the rest of the EU to 2.455 million tonnes from a previous target of 2.37 million tonnes.
The move was partly a balancing exercise to take account of a downward revision in domestic stocks at the end of the season triggered by a lack of barley going into intervention.
ONIC revised down its barley carryover stock estimate for June 30 to 829,000 tonnes from a previous 905,000 tonnes and the figure may have to reviewed again, one ONIC official said.
Normal operating stocks are closer to 600-700,000 tonnes.
However the closing stock forecast is higher than the 626,000 tonnes carried out in the previous July/June season.

For soft or common wheat, ONIC revised up its export estimate to EU countries to 9.36 million tonnes from a previous 9.185 million and projected maize exports from France to the rest of the EU of 6.75 million tonnes from 6.535 million tonnes.
In a separate report on EU grain balances for 1996/97, ONIC said total EU grain consumption reached 173.2 million tonnes, of which 105.9 million tonnes was to meet animal feed demand.
Overall consumption rose five percent from the previous year while the animal feed area was up six percent.
